questions.question:

questions.solution:

• The most appropriate answer for the given group of words is **'Exit poll'.**
 
• An **exit poll** is a survey of voters taken as they leave polling stations or voting booths, which is usually used for predicting the winners.
 
 
• *Example: The **exit poll** suggested that the incumbent candidate was likely to win the election by a significant margin.*

 
 
 

**Correct Answer:__** *Exit poll.*

• **Census**: Census is an official count or survey of a population, usually carried out by the government. (In Hindi, it is called जनगणना.)

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

questions.solution:

**Correct Sentence:__** ***Usually, Ratheesh doesn't** take part in these types of events because of his hectic schedule.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

They decided to have a meeting __to discuss about the project__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'to discuss the project'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'to discuss the project' **should be used instead of** 'to discuss about the project'.**
 
• The phrase **"to discuss about the project" **is not grammatically correct, as the verb** "discuss" **already implies that the following phrase will be the topic of discussion. Therefore, the preposition "**about**" is unnecessary and creates an error in the sentence.
 
• Let's see why other options are incorrect:
 
 
• The phrase *"to discuss through the project" *(**option 1**) does not convey the same meaning as the original sentence, as it suggests that the project itself will be used as a tool for discussion rather than being the topic of discussion.
 
• The phrase* "to discuss over the project" *(**option 3**) is not incorrect grammatically, but it is not as commonly used as *"to discuss the project" *and does not convey any additional meaning.
 
• The phrase *"to discuss beyond the project"* (**option 4**) suggests a discussion that extends beyond the boundaries or scope of the project, which is not the intended meaning of the original sentence.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *They decided to have a meeting **to discuss the project.***

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Suman was taking a nap.

options.text: A nap was being taken by Suman.
A nap has been taken by Suman.
A nap is being taken by Suman.
A nap was taken by Suman.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**A nap was being taken by Suman**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The given sentence is in the Active Voice. As per the given question we have to change the sentence into Passive Form. 
 
• The given sentence is an example of 'past continuous'. 
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
 
 
• Subject + was/were + V1+ing + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (Objective Case) + was/were+ being + V3 + by + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice) 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *He was riding a bike.*
 
• *A bike was being ridden by him. *
 
 
 
• Here, in the given sentence 'was taking' will be changed into 'was being taken'. 
 
• 'Suman' will be changed into the subject.
 
• 'A nap' will be changed into the object. 
 
• The preposition 'by' will be added. 

 
 
 

​Correct Sentence:__ *A nap was being taken by Suman.*

questions.question:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom **'Hold water'** is** 'Appear to be valid or reasonable'.**
 
• The idiom** 'hold water'** means to be valid, reasonable, or sound. It is often used to refer to an argument, theory, or explanation that appears to be valid or plausible. If an idea or argument does not **'hold water'**, it means it is **not logical or credible.**
 
 
• *Example: The explanation provided by the accused did not **hold water,** so the judge dismissed it and proceeded with the trial.*

 
 
 

**Correct Answer:__** *Appear to be valid or reasonable.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's see the origin of this idiom:
 
 
• The origin of idiom **"hold water" **is believed to have come from the ancient practice of carrying water in containers. In order for the container to be useful, it had to **"hold water" **without leaking or spilling.
 
• Therefore, if an argument or theory **"holds water,"** it is seen as being able to stand up to scrutiny and not fall apart, much like a container that holds water without leaking.
